about.title: San Rafael Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself — a faulty ladder, a malfunctioning kitchen appliance, a car part that fails on US-101, or a tool that breaks mid-use can turn an ordinary San Rafael afternoon into a trip to the ER. Marin County residents shop and work across a mix of small retailers, home-improvement stores, and online sellers, and any link in that chain — the manufacturer, distributor, or store — can potentially share responsibility when a product turns out to be unreasonably dangerous. California law gives injured consumers a real path forward here, and it doesn't hinge on proving someone was careless. If a product you used as intended caused you harm because of how it was designed, built, or labeled, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who reviews these cases and works on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand. Preserving the product itself matters, so hold onto it if you can.

whyChoose.title: Why San Rafael Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Ease Your Burden
items.desc: California generally applies strict liability to defective products, meaning you often don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which gives an attorney more avenues to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Design, Manufacturing, or Warning Defects All Count
items.desc: Whether the flaw was in how the product was engineered, built, or labeled, California law recognizes all three defect types as grounds for a claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability rules, you generally only need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that anyone acted negligently. An independent attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in its post-incident condition and avoid repairs or alterations. The product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in a defect claim, so store it safely until an attorney can review it.

items.question: I was hurt by a defective product near San Rafael's US-101 corridor or downtown shopping area — does location matter?
items.answer: Where the injury happened isn't usually the deciding factor in a product liability claim — what matters is the product's defect and the harm it caused. Still, local details like where you bought the item or where the incident occurred can help an attorney piece together your case.
